title: Ancestral plough use and women's labor-force participation
table: Table III, column 1: country-level female labor-force participation
unit: Country (one row per original country code)

original_reference.notes: Values printed in the authors' replicationcode_AGN.log for Table III, column 1. The corresponding Stata command is reg flfp2000 plow agricultural_suitability tropical_climate large_animals political_hierarchies economic_complexity, r. It includes an intercept and heteroskedasticity-robust HC1 standard errors.

id_country.description: World Bank country code retained from the original file.
id_country.units: Country code; identifier only, not a regression control

y.description: Female labor-force participation in 2000: percentage of women aged 15 to 64 in the labor force.
y.units: Percent (0 to 100); regression differences are percentage points

d.description: Population-weighted ancestral use of the animal plough, based on Ethnographic Atlas variable v39 and the authors' Ethnologue population mapping.
d.units: Share (0 to 1); continuous exposure, not a treatment indicator

x_agricultural_suitability.description: Ancestral agricultural suitability: share of land defined as suitable for the authors' cereal crops (millets, sorghum, wheat, barley and rye).

x_tropical_climate.description: Fraction of ancestral land in tropical or subtropical climates.

x_large_animals.description: Ancestral presence of large domesticated animals.

x_political_hierarchies.description: Ancestral jurisdictional hierarchy beyond the local community, using the authors' coding of Ethnographic Atlas variable v33.
x_political_hierarchies.units: Population-weighted index (1 to 5), not a count of modern governments

x_economic_complexity.description: Ancestral settlement-pattern index from Ethnographic Atlas variable v30; higher values indicate more complex settlements.
x_economic_complexity.units: Population-weighted index (1 to 8), not monetary income

sample_notes: The original file has 234 rows; retain the 177 complete cases on the outcome, exposure and five original controls.
Preserve original row order and values; no imputation, rescaling, trimming or additional sample restriction is applied.
The regression includes an intercept, with no weights, fixed effects or clustering; use HC1 standard errors.
This is the country-level Table III, column 1 exercise. The paper's separate WVS Table V, column 4 analysis concerns individual attitudes about scarce jobs and is not used here.
identification_notes: This observational OLS specification measures a cross-country conditional association. The OLS estimate alone does not establish exogenous ancestral plough use.
The coefficient is in labor-force-participation percentage points for a one-unit (zero-to-one) change in ancestral plough-use share.
The paper's instrumental-variable specifications are separate analyses and are not implemented here.

source.attribution: Alesina, Alberto; Giuliano, Paola; Nunn, Nathan (2013). On the Origins of Gender Roles: Women and the Plough. Quarterly Journal of Economics 128(2):469–530.
